contents.html: On April 9 and 10, 1991 the Protocol Security Group at NIST held its Second Workshop on Security Labels. Forty representatives from the U.S. Government, Industry, and the Canadian Government gathered for two days to discuss a NIST proposed Standard Security Label for the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. Issues on security policy and security object registration were also discussed in reference to the proposed label. The information shared during the two days of discussion and the recommendations of the group are documented in these proceedings.
contents.html_ja: 1991 年 4 月 9 日と 10 日に、NIST のプロトコルセキュリティグループは、セキュリティラベルに関する第 2 回ワークショップを開催しました。米国政府、産業界、カナダ政府から 40 人の代表が 2 日間にわたって集まり、NIST が提案した米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile）向けの標準セキュリティラベルについて議論しました。提案されたラベルに関連して、セキュリティポリシーとセキュリティオブジェクト登録に関する課題も議論されました。2 日間の議論で共有された情報と、グループの勧告は、この会議録に記録されています。

contents.html: Robert Rosenthal, Manager of the Protocol Security Group at NIST, welcomed the attendees. He described the role of this workshop in NIST's effort to incorporate security mechanisms into the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. Mr. Rosenthal envisions a set of Government OSI Security Profiles that will be pointed to by the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 146, GOSIP. The first set of profiles would include the following topics:
contents.html_ja: NIST のプロトコルセキュリティグループのマネージャーである Robert Rosenthal が、参加者を歓迎しました。同氏は、NIST が米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイルにセキュリティ機構を組み込む取り組みの中での、このワークショップの役割を説明しました。Rosenthal 氏は、連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）146（GOSIP）が参照する一連の政府 OSI セキュリティプロファイルを構想しています。最初のプロファイル群には、次のトピックが含まれる予定です。

contents.html: Larry Keys (NIST), will be the Registrar for NIST's Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR). The CSOR is being organized using ANSI/ISO guidelines for object registration. Mr. Keys gave a status report on the work done so far in setting up this service and outlined the basics of the registration procedure.

contents.html: George Rogers (IC Staff) asked whether this register could or would register classified objects. contents.html: Ron Sharp (AT&T) represented the Trusted Systems Interoperability Group (TSIG). Mr. Sharp described the TSIG as a very informal group of implementors interested in developing interoperable trusted distributed systems. The TSIG is engaged in projects such as CIPSO, Trusted X-Windows, Trusted Network File Systems (NFS), Trusted Session Management, and Trusted Sockets. The current focus for TSIG members is the TCP/IP communications protocol but the door remains open for a transition to OSI as markets emerge. In developing CIPSO the TSIG adopted and modified original work done by Sun Microsystems and Hewlett-Packard. The group has spawned an Internet Working Group whose purpose is to present CIPSO as an Internet Request for Comment (RFC). Mr. Sharp enumerated reasons for the development of CIPSO, its main features, and presented the label format. His presentation slides and the current version of the CIPSO specification appears on page 55 of this document.
contents.html_ja: Ron Sharp（AT&T）は、Trusted Systems Interoperability Group（TSIG）を代表しました。Sharp 氏は、TSIG を、相互運用可能な信頼できる分散システムの開発に関心を持つ実装者による、非常に非公式なグループだと説明しました。TSIG は、CIPSO、Trusted X-Windows、Trusted Network File Systems（NFS）、Trusted Session Management、Trusted Sockets などのプロジェクトに取り組んでいます。TSIG メンバーの現在の焦点は TCP/IP 通信プロトコルですが、市場が形成されるにつれて OSI に移行する可能性も残されています。CIPSO の開発にあたり、TSIG は Sun Microsystems と Hewlett-Packard が行った元の作業を採用し、修正しました。このグループからは、CIPSO を Internet Request for Comment（RFC）として提示することを目的とする Internet Working Group が生まれています。Sharp 氏は、CIPSO の開発理由と主な特徴を列挙し、ラベル形式を提示しました。同氏の発表スライドと CIPSO 仕様の現行版は、この文書の55ページに掲載されています。

contents.html: Noel Nazario presented the Standard Security Label (SSL). The specification for this label is given by the initial draft of a FIPS, called Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. This document provides the format of a security label that may be used at different layers of the OSI architecture. The semantics of the label will be given by a Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR). This future FIPS will be referenced by the U. S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP) when describing labeling options for various protocols.
contents.html_ja: Noel Nazario は、標準セキュリティラベル（SSL）を発表しました。このラベルの仕様は、Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile という FIPS の最初の草案で示されています。この文書は、OSI アーキテクチャのさまざまな層で使用できるセキュリティラベルの形式を提供します。ラベルの意味論は、Computer Security Objects Register（CSOR）によって与えられます。この将来の FIPS は、さまざまなプロトコルのラベル付けの選択肢を記述する際に、米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（GOSIP）から参照されます。

contents.html: The SSL begins with a Security Label Indicator and a length field indicating the length of the Security Information that follows. The Security Information field includes a Register Index Code (RIC), a Security Level field, and Security Tags. The RIC identifies the semantic rules for the label as registered in the CSOR. There are four tag types, one of which indicates the end of the label. The other three tag types may be used to carry additional security information. The presentation slides on page 21 of this report illustrate the general format of the label and the four tag types. A full description appears in the draft FIPS text also included.
contents.html_ja: SSL は、セキュリティラベル識別子と、それに続くセキュリティ情報の長さを示す長さフィールドで始まります。セキュリティ情報フィールドには、レジスタ索引コード（RIC）、セキュリティレベルフィールド、セキュリティタグが含まれます。RIC は、CSOR に登録されたラベルの意味規則を識別します。タグの種類は 4 つあり、そのうち 1 つはラベルの終端を示します。残りの 3 つのタグの種類は、追加のセキュリティ情報を運ぶために使うことができます。この報告書の 21 ページの発表スライドは、ラベルの一般的な形式と 4 つのタグの種類を示しています。完全な説明は、同じく掲載されている FIPS 草案の本文にあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。分かれた段落を原本どおりにまとめる

contents.html: Mr. Nazario compared the label option currently specified by GOSIP for the Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) to the SSL. The GOSIP CLNP security option is actually two separate options defined by two different authorities or activities while the SSL can provide the same information in a label defined by a single authority. The Classification Protection Level in the Basic Security Option (BSO) is analogous to the Security Level field in the SSL. The equivalent of the Additional Security Information in the Extended Security Option (ESO) can be provided by the three information-carrying tag types in the SSL.
contents.html_ja: Nazario 氏は、現在 GOSIP がコネクションレスネットワークプロトコル（CLNP）向けに規定しているラベルのオプションを、SSL と比較しました。GOSIP の CLNP セキュリティオプションは、実際には 2 つの異なる機関または活動によって定義された 2 つの別個のオプションですが、SSL は、単一の機関が定義するラベルで同じ情報を提供できます。基本セキュリティオプション（BSO）の分類保護レベル（Classification Protection Level）は、SSL のセキュリティレベルフィールドに相当します。拡張セキュリティオプション（ESO）の追加セキュリティ情報（Additional Security Information）に相当するものは、SSL の 3 つの情報搬送用タグ型で提供できます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: Mr. Nazario also compared the SSL to the Commercial CIPSO. There are two main distinctions between the CIPSO label and the SSL. The Domain of Interpretation field that identifies the defining authority for the CIPSO label is a four octet fixed length field while the RIC, which points to the semantics of the label as registered in the CSOR for the SSL, is a variable length field. The second difference is that every CIPSO tag has a security level field while there is only one security level field in the SSL.
contents.html_ja: Nazario 氏は、SSL を商用の CIPSO とも比較しました。CIPSO のラベルと SSL の間には、2 つの主な違いがあります。CIPSO のラベルの定義機関を識別する解釈ドメイン（Domain of Interpretation）フィールドは 4 オクテットの固定長フィールドですが、SSL では CSOR に登録されたラベルの意味論を指す RIC が可変長フィールドです。2 つ目の違いは、CIPSO ではすべてのタグにセキュリティレベルフィールドがあるのに対し、SSL ではセキュリティレベルフィールドが 1 つしかないことです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: Noel Nazario also presented proposed modifications to the text in the security chapter (6) of the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). Chapter 6 of GOSIP currently contains the specification for a security option for the Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP). This chapter is also a placeholder for future specifications. Changes include a new paragraph structure to accommodate a NIST Security Information option for CLNP and placeholders for security parameters at other layers. Only a label parameter is currently defined within the NIST Security Information option. A pointer to the SSL document provides the format specification for this label parameter. The new text also points to the Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR) to provide the semantics for the label. The new CLNP Security Parameter allows the use of either the existent BSO/ESO label or the NIST Security Information. The BSO/ESO was kept for backwards compatibility.
contents.html_ja: Noel Nazario は、米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（GOSIP）のセキュリティの章（第 6 章）の本文に対する、修正案も発表しました。GOSIP の第 6 章には現在、コネクションレスネットワークプロトコル（CLNP）向けのセキュリティオプションの仕様が含まれています。この章は、将来の仕様のための場所としても確保されています。変更点には、CLNP 向けの NIST セキュリティ情報オプションに対応するための新しい段落構成と、他の層のセキュリティパラメータのための場所の確保が含まれます。NIST セキュリティ情報オプションの中で現在定義されているのは、ラベルパラメータだけです。SSL 文書へのポインタが、このラベルパラメータの形式仕様を提供します。新しい本文は、ラベルの意味論を提供する Computer Security Objects Register（CSOR）も指しています。新しい CLNP セキュリティパラメータでは、既存の BSO/ESO ラベルか NIST セキュリティ情報のいずれかを使用できます。BSO/ESO は、後方互換性のために残されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。語順が崩れた断片を原本の読み順でまとめる

contents.html: Wayne Jansen (NIST) presented an overview of Security Labels at the Transport Layer. His discussion dealt with the Transport Layer Security Protocol (TLSP). The TLSP, currently under development within ISO, is being balloted for CD (Committee Draft) status. Mr. Jansen compared the SSL and the TLSP label formats and their respective views on label registration. The presentation suggested a compromise format for the alignment of both labels and a methodology for creating label definitions independent of encoding concerns using ASN.1.
contents.html_ja: Wayne Jansen（NIST）は、トランスポート層のセキュリティラベルの概要を発表しました。同氏の議論は、トランスポート層セキュリティプロトコル（TLSP）を扱うものでした。TLSP は現在 ISO で策定中で、CD（Committee Draft）の段階に向けた投票が行われています。Jansen 氏は、SSL と TLSP のラベル形式、およびそれぞれのラベル登録についての見解を比較しました。発表では、両方のラベルを整合させるための折衷的な形式と、ASN.1 を用いて符号化の問題と独立にラベル定義を作成する方法論が提案されました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ASN.l を ASN.1 に直す

contents.html: Russ Housley (Xerox) presented comments on the draft Standard Security Label document. The proposed label may be applicable to several protocols within the OSI architecture. However, an ASN.1 definition would be necessary for use at layer 7. The IEEE 802.2 working group is currently working on a layer 2 label, it would be appropriate to present the SSL to that group. Mr. Housley added that there should be a reference in the SSL text that indicates what document provides usage rules for this label. The full text of the Xerox comments appear later in this document.
contents.html_ja: Russ Housley（Xerox）は、標準セキュリティラベル文書の草案についてのコメントを発表しました。提案されたラベルは、OSI アーキテクチャ内の複数のプロトコルに適用される場合があります。ただし、レイヤ 7 で使用するには、ASN.1 による定義が必要になります。IEEE 802.2 ワーキンググループは現在、レイヤ 2 のラベルに取り組んでおり、SSL をそのグループに提示するのが適切です。Housley 氏は、このラベルの使用規則を提供する文書を示す参照を、SSL の本文に入れるべきだと付け加えました。Xerox のコメントの全文は、この文書の後ろのほうにあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ASN.l を ASN.1 に直す

contents.html: Hilary Hosmer (Data Security) presented the concept of multipolicy. She pointed out that OSI security labels should be able to support co-existing security policies . Ms. Hosmer stated that allowing only one Security Level field in the SSL is a serious limitation because it makes it difficult to support multiple security policies.
contents.html_ja: Hilary Hosmer（Data Security）は、マルチポリシーの概念を発表しました。同氏は、OSI のセキュリティラベルは、共存する複数のセキュリティポリシーをサポートできるべきだと指摘しました。Hosmer 氏は、SSL にセキュリティレベルフィールドが 1 つしか認められていないことは、複数のセキュリティポリシーをサポートしにくくするため、重大な制約であると述べました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ずれたピリオドを原本の位置に戻す

contents.html: David Crawford (Canadian Defense) discussed Canada's coexisting security policies. He explained the relationship between security levels that cover the equivalents to U.S. Classified and Unclassified but Sensitive.
contents.html_ja: David Crawford（Canadian Defense）は、カナダの共存するセキュリティポリシーについて論じました。同氏は、米国の Classified（機密）と Unclassified but Sensitive（非機密だが機微）に相当するものをカバーするセキュリティレベルの関係を説明しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。Canada *s を Canada's に直す

contents.html: Thomas Bartee (IC Staff) presented a position paper justifying a request for an additional tag type for the Standard Security Label (SSL). Mr. Bartee's argument was that the tags currently specified in the SSL are geared towards indicating restriction markings. The addition of a "reversed" bit map type would make it easier to specify permissive markings such as release indicators. He mentioned that such an approach is currently used in the Director of Central Intelligence Office (DCI) Extended IP Security Option and by the Compartmented Workstation program.
contents.html_ja: Thomas Bartee（IC Staff）は、標準セキュリティラベル（SSL）にタグ型を追加する要請を正当化する意見書を発表しました。Bartee 氏の主張は、SSL で現在規定されているタグは、制限のマーキングを示すことに向けられているというものでした。「反転」ビットマップ型を追加すれば、公開指示などの許容的なマーキングを指定しやすくなります。同氏は、このような手法が、Director of Central Intelligence Office（DCI）の拡張 IP セキュリティオプションと、Compartmented Workstation プログラムで現在使われていることに言及しました。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。分かれた段落を原本どおりにまとめる

contents.html: The Federal Information Processing Standards Publication Series of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is the official series of publications relating to standards and guidelines adopted and promulgated under the provisions of Section 111(d) of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 as amended by the Computer Security Act of 1987, Public Law 100-235. These mandates have given the Secretary of Commerce and NIST important responsibilities for improving the utilization and management of computer and related telecommunications systems in the Federal Government. The NIST, through the Computer Systems Laboratory, provides leadership , technical guidance, and coordination of Government efforts in the development of standards and guidelines in these areas.
contents.html_ja: 国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の連邦情報処理標準刊行物シリーズは、1987 年コンピュータセキュリティ法（公法 100-235）によって改正された、1949 年連邦財産・行政サービス法（Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949）第 111 条(d) の規定に基づいて採択され公布された標準とガイドラインに関する、公式の刊行物シリーズです。これらの法令により、商務長官と NIST は、連邦政府におけるコンピュータおよび関連する電気通信システムの利用と管理を改善するための重要な責任を負っています。NIST は、コンピュータシステム研究所を通じて、これらの分野における標準とガイドラインの策定に関する政府の取り組みについて、リーダーシップ、技術的指針、調整を提供しています。

contents.html: This Standard specifies the format for a security label for the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). This network security label tells protocol processing entities how to handle unclassified but sensitive data communicated between open systems. Information carried by this label can be used to control access, specify protective measures, and indicate additional handling restrictions required by a network security policy.
contents.html_ja: この標準は、米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（GOSIP）向けのセキュリティラベルの形式を規定します。このネットワークセキュリティラベルは、開放型システム間で通信される非機密だが機微なデータをどのように扱うかを、プロトコル処理エンティティに伝えます。このラベルが運ぶ情報は、アクセスの制御、保護措置の指定、およびネットワークセキュリティポリシーが求める追加の取り扱い制限の指示に使うことができます。

contents.html: Explanation: This Standard specifies the format for a security Label within the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). Security labels indicate data sensitivity to accidental, unauthorized, intentional, or malicious disclosure, modification and destruction. Labels are used to control access, specify protective measures, and indicate handling restrictions required by a network security policy.
contents.html_ja: 説明: この標準は、米国政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（GOSIP）におけるセキュリティラベルの形式を規定します。セキュリティラベルは、偶発的、無許可、意図的、または悪意のある開示、変更、破壊に対するデータの機微性を示します。ラベルは、アクセスの制御、保護措置の指定、およびネットワークセキュリティポリシーが求める取り扱い制限の指示に使います。

contents.html: The label presented here contains a security level indicator and security tags that may carry compartments, caveats, and handling restrictions. Four security tag types provide for a bit map, two enumerated set representations (set inclusion and set exclusion), and a free form field.
contents.html_ja: ここで示すラベルは、セキュリティレベル識別子と、コンパートメント、注意書き、取り扱い制限を運ぶことができるセキュリティタグを含みます。4 つのセキュリティタグ型により、ビットマップ、2 つの列挙集合表現（集合への包含と集合からの除外）、および自由形式フィールドを提供します。

contents.html: Scope: This standard specifies a security label for GOSIP compliant implementations. The specified label may be used as a security feature at different layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The specification given here is limited to the syntactic aspect of the label. The semantics of security labels, as defined for different security domains, are given by a Security Objects Register. Appendix B contains an example semantic definition for a label.
contents.html_ja: 適用範囲: この標準は、GOSIP に準拠した実装のためのセキュリティラベルを規定します。規定されたラベルは、開放型システム間相互接続（OSI）アーキテクチャのさまざまな層で、セキュリティ機能として使用できます。ここで示す仕様は、ラベルの構文面に限られます。さまざまなセキュリティドメインに対して定義されるセキュリティラベルの意味論は、Security Objects Register によって与えられます。付録 B に、ラベルの意味定義の例があります。

contents.html: Applicability: The specified label applies to OSI network systems handling U.S. Government unclassified but sensitive data. This includes use by government agencies and commercial organizations conducting business with the Federal government.

contents.html: U.S. Government agencies are required to protect information assets essential to their operations. This includes both the protection of information within computer systems and while in transit over communications networks. This standard defines a network security label for use with the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Profile (GOSIP; FIPS PUB XXX).

contents.html: The security label specified here can indicate data sensitivity to accidental, unauthorized, intentional, or malicious disclosure, modification and destruction. This label can also help to control access, specify protective measures, and indicate handling restrictions required by the network security policy.

contents.html: Additional security information is conveyed using Security Tags. A single label may have multiple variable size tags. Each Security Tag has fixed size type and length fields plus a variable size information field. The value of the length field in Tag Type 0 is zero; it contains no information.
contents.html_ja: 追加のセキュリティ情報は、セキュリティタグを使って伝達されます。1 つのラベルは、複数の可変サイズのタグを持つことができます。各セキュリティタグは、固定サイズの型フィールドと長さフィールド、および可変サイズの情報フィールドを持ちます。タグ型 0 の長さフィールドの値はゼロで、情報を含みません。

contents.html: The size of the Additional Security Tag Type (TT) field is 1 octet. Its value indicates the tag type. Values range between 0 and 255. This standard defines tag types 0 through 4, all other tag types are reserved for definition by NIST's Security Objects Register. At least one tag must be present in every label.
contents.html_ja: 追加セキュリティタグ型（TT）フィールドのサイズは 1 オクテットです。その値はタグ型を示します。値の範囲は 0 から 255 です。この標準はタグ型 0 から 4 を定義し、それ以外のすべてのタグ型は、NIST の Security Objects Register による定義のために予約されています。すべてのラベルには、少なくとも 1 つのタグが存在しなければなりません。

contents.html: The information carried by this tag is interpreted as a bit map of security attributes. The complete set of possible attributes is represented and those that apply are explicitly indicated. Length field values range between 1 and 30 octets.
contents.html_ja: このタグが運ぶ情報は、セキュリティ属性のビットマップとして解釈されます。取りうる属性の全集合が表され、適用されるものが明示的に示されます。長さフィールドの値は、1 から 30 オクテットの範囲です。

contents.html: In the bit map a bit N is set to 1 if attribute N (as defined in the register), is part of the label it is 0 if attribute N is not part of the label. Bits shall be numbered starting with the most significant bit of the first transmitted octet. Unused bits at the end the last octet are set to 0.
contents.html_ja: ビットマップでは、属性 N（レジスタで定義されたもの）がラベルの一部であればビット N を 1 に設定し、そうでなければ 0 に設定します。ビットには、最初に送信されるオクテットの最上位ビットから番号を付けなければなりません。最後のオクテットの末尾にある未使用ビットは 0 に設定します。

contents.html: Tag type 2 is used when only a few security attributes out of a large set apply to a protocol data unit (PDU). This is done by enumerating the attributes that apply (set inclusion). contents.html: 4.5 Usage Rules

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: At most 1 security label may be used per layer PDU. The label described here shall be copied upon fragmentation. All multi-octet fields are defined to be transmitted in network byte order.
contents.html_ja: 層の PDU ごとに使用できるセキュリティラベルは、最大 1 つです。ここで記述するラベルは、フラグメンテーション時にコピーしなければなりません。すべての複数オクテットのフィールドは、ネットワークバイトオーダーで送信されるものと定義されています。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: At least one tag must be present in every label. If no additional security information is required a NULL tag (Type 0) will be used. Only 1 NULL tag may appear in any label, it indicates the end of the label. The failure to find a NULL tag when expected and/or the finding of such tag when not expected are security relevant events that must be reported.
contents.html_ja: すべてのラベルには、少なくとも 1 つのタグが存在しなければなりません。追加のセキュリティ情報が必要ない場合は、NULL タグ（型 0）を使用します。どのラベルにも NULL タグは最大 1 つまで現れてよく、ラベルの終端を示します。期待される位置に NULL タグが見つからないこと、および／または期待されない位置にそのようなタグが見つかることは、報告しなければならないセキュリティ関連事象です。

contents.html: ASN.1 Definition for Standard Security Label
contents.html_ja: 標準セキュリティラベルの ASN.1 定義
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ASN.l を直す

contents.html:
Standard Security Label ::= IMPLICIT  SEQUENCE {
      registerindexcode       RegisterIndexCode,
      securityLevel           OCTET STRING (SIZE(1)),
      securityTags            SEQUENCE OF SecurityTag OPTIONAL    }

RegisterIndexCode       ::= IMPLICIT  OCTET STRING

SecurityTag             ::= CHOICE  {
-- Type 0
      nulltag                       [0] IMPLICIT OCTET STRING (SIZE(0)),
-- Type 1
      bitMap                        [1] IMPLICIT OCTET STRING (SIZE(1..30)),
-- Type 2
      enumeratedAttributes          [2] IMPLICIT  SET OF SecurityAttribute,
-- Type 3
      complimentaryEnumAttributes   [3] IMPLICIT  SET OF  SecurityAttribute,
-- Type 4
      freeFormField                 [4] IMPLICIT  OCTET STRING (SIZE(1..30)) }

SecurityAttribute ::= IMPLICIT OCTET STRING (SIZE(2))
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ASN.1 定義を原本画像（scale 3）から字下げどおりに起こす（OCR は語順が崩れ、SIZE(l)・SIZE(O) など誤認あり）

contents.html: Security is of fundamental importance to the acceptance and use of open systems in the U.S. Government. Part 2 of the Open Systems Interconnection reference model (Security Architecture) is now an International Standard (IS 7498/2). The standard describes a general architecture for security in OSI, defines a set of security services that may be supported within the OSI model, and outlines a number of mechanisms than can be used in providing the services. However, no protocols, formats or minimum requirements are contained in the standard.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティは、米国政府における開放型システムの受け入れと使用にとって根本的に重要です。OSI 参照モデルの第 2 部（セキュリティアーキテクチャ）は、現在、国際標準（IS 7498/2）となっています。この標準は、OSI におけるセキュリティの一般的なアーキテクチャを記述し、OSI モデル内でサポートされる場合がある一連のセキュリティサービスを定義し、それらのサービスを提供するために使用できる複数の機構の概要を示しています。しかし、この標準には、プロトコル、形式、最小要件は含まれていません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ずれたピリオドを直す（"than can be used" は原本どおり）
contents.translation_resolve_note: 現在の訳で英文の意味・要件語・用語が正しい。指摘は誤りまたは文体の好み

contents.html: The text below describes security options that may be specified when incorporating security services to OSI Network and Transport Layers. This chapter does not describe at this time a complete set of security options that a user might desire nor a description of the security services and protocols that are associated with the specified parameters. Security labels are parameters that have been identified as needed if certain security services (e.g., confidentiality, access control) are incorporated to the OSI Layers. This chapter should be considered as a placeholder for future security specifications. Appendix 1 provides further information on what specifications are considered needed for OSI security.
contents.html_ja: 以下の本文は、セキュリティサービスを OSI のネットワーク層とトランスポート層に組み込む際に指定してもよいセキュリティオプションを記述します。この章では現時点で、利用者が望む可能性のあるセキュリティオプションの完全な集合も、指定されたパラメータに関連するセキュリティサービスとプロトコルの説明も示していません。セキュリティラベルは、特定のセキュリティサービス（例: 機密性、アクセス制御）を OSI の層に組み込む場合に必要と特定されたパラメータです。この章は、将来のセキュリティ仕様のための暫定的な位置付けとみなすべきです。付録 1 は、OSI セキュリティに必要と考えられる仕様について、さらに詳しい情報を提供します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。分かれた段落を原本どおりにまとめる

contents.html: As defined by ISO, security features are considered both implementation and usage options. An organization desiring security in a product that is being purchased in accordance with this profile must specify the security services required, the placement of the services within the OSI architecture, the mechanisms to provide the services and the management features required.
contents.html_ja: ISO が定義するとおり、セキュリティ機能は、実装のオプションと使用のオプションの両方とみなされます。このプロファイルに従って購入する製品にセキュリティを求める組織は、必要なセキュリティサービス、OSI アーキテクチャ内でのサービスの配置、サービスを提供する機構、および必要な管理機能を規定しなければなりません。

contents.html: The implementation of the security option requires assigning new parameter values to the Reason for Discard parameter in the CLNP Error Report PDU. The first octet of the parameter value contains an error type code as described in IS 8473. Values beyond those assigned in the standard are shown in Table 6.1. The second octet of the Reason for Discard parameter value either locates the error in the discarded PDU or contains the value zero as described in the standard.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティオプションの実装では、CLNP エラーレポート PDU の破棄理由（Reason for Discard）パラメータに、新しいパラメータ値を割り当てる必要があります。パラメータ値の最初のオクテットには、IS 8473 に記述されたエラー型コードが入ります。標準で割り当てられたもの以外の値は、表 6.1 に示します。破棄理由パラメータ値の 2 番目のオクテットは、標準に記述されたとおり、破棄された PDU 内のエラーの位置を示すか、値ゼロを含みます。

contents.html: The Basic Security Option of the Security Parameter identifies the U.S. Department of Defense classification level to which a PDU is to be protected and the authorities whose protection rules apply to that PDU. This option may appear at most once in a PDU. When the Basic Security Option appears in the Security Parameter of a PDU, it must be the first option in the Parameter Value field. This parameter may not be used together with the NIST Security Option. Section 6.2.3 defines the format of the Basic Security Option.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティパラメータの基本セキュリティオプションは、PDU の保護対象となる米国国防総省の分類レベルと、その PDU に保護規則が適用される機関を識別します。このオプションは、1 つの PDU に最大 1 回しか現れません。基本セキュリティオプションが PDU のセキュリティパラメータに現れる場合、それはパラメータ値フィールドの最初のオプションでなければなりません。このパラメータは、NIST セキュリティオプションと併用できません。基本セキュリティオプションの形式は、第 6.2.3 節で定義されています。

contents.html: The Extended Security Option permits additional security labelling information beyond that present in the Basic Security Option. This extended information is supplied in a CLNP or Connection Oriented Transport PDU to meet the needs of registered authorities. This option may appear at most once in a PDU. The Extended Security Option must follow the Basic Option if it is present in the Security Parameter Value field. If an authority requires this option for a specific system, it must be specified explicitly in any Request for Proposal for that system. This parameter may not be used together with the NIST Security Option. Paragraph 6.2.4 defines the format of the Extended Option.
contents.html_ja: 拡張セキュリティオプションは、基本セキュリティオプションにある情報を超える追加のセキュリティラベル情報を提供します。この拡張情報は、登録された機関のニーズを満たすために、CLNP またはコネクション型トランスポートの PDU で提供されます。このオプションは、1 つの PDU に最大 1 回しか現れません。セキュリティパラメータ値フィールドに基本オプションが存在する場合、拡張セキュリティオプションはその後に続かなければなりません。ある機関が特定のシステムにこのオプションを必要とする場合は、そのシステムの提案依頼書（Request for Proposal）に明示的に規定しなければなりません。このパラメータは、NIST セキュリティオプションと併用できません。拡張オプションの形式は、第 6.2.4 項で定義されています。

contents.html: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Security Option provides for a number of network security related parameters. The NIST Security Label is the only parameter type currently defined under this option. This parameter is specified in FIPS PUB XXX, Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. The NIST Security Label parameter provides a security level indicator and security information tags to convey security information on CLNP or Connection Oriented Transport PDUs. NIST reserves all other NIST Security Option parameter types. The security label parameter option may appear at most once in a PDU. This parameter may not be used together with the Basic and/or Extended Security Options. If this option is required by an authority for a specific system, it must be specified explicitly in any Request for Proposal for that system. Paragraph 6.2.5 defines the format of the NIST Security Option.
contents.html_ja: 国立標準技術研究所（NIST）セキュリティオプションは、ネットワークセキュリティに関連する複数のパラメータを提供します。このオプションのもとで現在定義されているパラメータ型は、NIST セキュリティラベルだけです。このパラメータは、FIPS PUB XXX、Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile で規定されています。NIST セキュリティラベルパラメータは、CLNP またはコネクション型トランスポートの PDU でセキュリティ情報を伝えるための、セキュリティレベル識別子とセキュリティ情報タグを提供します。NIST は、NIST セキュリティオプションのその他すべてのパラメータ型を予約しています。セキュリティラベルパラメータオプションは、1 つの PDU に最大 1 回しか現れません。このパラメータは、基本および／または拡張セキュリティオプションと併用できません。ある機関が特定のシステムにこのオプションを必要とする場合は、そのシステムの提案依頼書に明示的に規定しなければなりません。NIST セキュリティオプションの形式は、第 6.2.5 節で定義されています。

contents.html: The Protection Authority Flags field indicates the National Access Program(s) or Special Access Program(s) whose rules apply to the protection of the PDU. Its field length and source flags are described below. To maintain the architectural consistency and interoperability of DoD common user data networks, users of these networks should submit requirements for additional Protection Authority Flags to DCA DISDB, Washington, D. C. 20305-2000 for review and approval.
contents.html_ja: 保護機関フラグフィールドは、PDU の保護に規則が適用される国家アクセスプログラムまたは特別アクセスプログラムを示します。このフィールドの長さと保護機関フラグについて、以下で説明します。国防総省の共通利用者データネットワークのアーキテクチャ上の一貫性と相互運用性を維持するため、これらのネットワークの利用者は、追加の保護機関フラグに関する要件を、レビューと承認のために DCA DISDB, Washington, D. C. 20305-2000 に提出すべきです。

contents.html: A. Field Length: The Protection Authority Flags field is variable in length. The low order bit (Bit 1) of an octet is encoded as "0" if the octet is the final octet in the field. If there are additional octets, then the low order bit is encoded as "1". Currently, there are less than eight authorities. Therefore, only one octet is required and the low order bit of this octet is encoded as "0".
contents.html_ja: A. フィールドの長さ: 保護機関フラグフィールドは可変長です。オクテットの最下位ビット（ビット 1）は、そのオクテットがフィールドの最後のオクテットである場合は「0」に符号化されます。追加のオクテットがある場合は、最下位ビットは「1」に符号化されます。現在、機関は 8 未満です。したがって、必要なオクテットは 1 つだけで、このオクテットの最下位ビットは「0」に符号化されます。

contents.html: B. Source Flags: Bits 2 through 8 in each octet are flags. Each flag is associated with an authority as indicated in Table 6.7. The bit corresponding to an authority is "1" if the PDU is to be protected in accordance with the rules of that authority.
contents.html_ja: B. 送信元フラグ: 各オクテットのビット 2〜8 がフラグです。各フラグは、表 6.7 に示すとおり、機関に関連付けられます。機関に対応するビットは、PDU がその機関の規則に従って保護される場合に「1」になります。

contents.html: The value of the Additional Security Information Format Code corresponds to a particular format and meaning for a specific Additional Security Information field. Each format code is assigned to a specific controlling activity. Once assigned, this activity becomes the authority for the definition of the remainder of the Additional Security Information identified by that format code. A single controlling activity may be responsible for multiple format codes. However, a particular format code may appear at most once in a PDU. For each Additional Security Information Format Code an authority is responsible for, that authority will provide sufficient criteria for determining whether a CLNP PDU marked with its Format Code should be accepted or rejected. Whenever possible, this criteria will be Unclassified.
contents.html_ja: 追加セキュリティ情報形式コードの値は、特定の追加セキュリティ情報フィールドに固有の形式と意味に対応します。各形式コードは、特定の管理活動に割り当てられます。割り当てられると、この活動は、その形式コードで識別される追加セキュリティ情報の残りの部分を定義する権限を持ちます。1 つの管理活動が複数の形式コードに責任を負う場合があります。ただし、特定の形式コードは、1 つの PDU に最大 1 回だけ現れます。機関が責任を負う各追加セキュリティ情報形式コードについて、その機関は、自らの形式コードが付された CLNP PDU を受理すべきか拒否すべきかを判断するための十分な基準を提供します。可能な限り、この基準は Unclassified とします。

contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: C. A PDU whose security level is greater than the end system's maximum security level, then:
contents.html_ja: C. PDU のセキュリティレベルがエンドシステムの最大セキュリティレベルを上回る場合は、次のようにします。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: 1. If a CLNP Error Report PDU triggered the Out-of-Range condition, then no reply is permitted and the PDU should be discarded. A CLNP Error Report PDU must not be sent in this case.
contents.html_ja: 1. CLNP エラーレポート PDU が範囲外の状態を引き起こした場合は、応答は許可されず、PDU を破棄すべきです。この場合、CLNP エラーレポート PDU を送信してはなりません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。番号「1.」を補い、分かれた段落をまとめる

contents.html: 2. Otherwise, discard the PDU and send a CLNP Error Report PDU to the originating CLNP entity. The first octet of the Reason for Discard parameter is set as specified in Table 6.1. The second octet of the Reason for Discard parameter identifies the Out-of-Range Security Option. It should point to the first octet (i.e., the type indicator) of the Out-of-Range option. Alternatively, the second octet can be set to zero. The response is sent at the maximum classification level of the end system which received the PDU. The protection authority flags are set to be the intersection of those for which the host is accredited and those present in the PDU which triggered this response.
contents.html_ja: 2. そうでない場合は、PDU を破棄し、発信元の CLNP エンティティに CLNP エラーレポート PDU を送信します。破棄理由（Reason for Discard）パラメータの最初のオクテットは、表 6.1 に規定されたとおりに設定します。破棄理由パラメータの 2 番目のオクテットは、範囲外のセキュリティオプションを識別します。これは、範囲外のオプションの最初のオクテット（つまり、型識別子）を指すべきです。あるいは、2 番目のオクテットをゼロに設定することもできます。応答は、PDU を受信したエンドシステムの最大分類レベルで送信されます。保護機関フラグは、ホストが認定されているものと、この応答を引き起こした PDU に存在するものの共通部分に設定されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。番号「2.」を補い、分かれた段落をまとめる

Reply = "Unclassified, GENSER".
contents.html_ja:
例: PDU = 「Secret, GENSER」
エンドシステムのレベル = 「Unclassified, GENSER」。

contents.html: These are the least restrictive actions permitted by this protocol. Individual end systems, system administrators, or protection authorities may impose more stringent restrictions on responses and in some instances may not permit any response at all to a PDU which is outside the accredited security range of an end system.
contents.html_ja: これらは、このプロトコルで許可される、最も制限の緩やかな措置です。個々のエンドシステム、システム管理者、または保護機関は、応答についてより厳しい制限を課す場合があり、場合によっては、エンドシステムの認定済みセキュリティ範囲の外にある PDU に対して、いかなる応答も許可しないことがあります。

contents.html: 6.2.8 Trusted Intermediary Procedure for communications protected by the Basic and Extended Security Options.
contents.html_ja: 6.2.8 基本セキュリティオプションおよび拡張セキュリティオプションで保護された通信のための、信頼できる仲介者の手続
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本画像と語ごとに照合

contents.html: Certain devices in an internetwork may act as intermediaries to validate that communications between two end systems is authorized. This decision is based on a combination of knowledge of the end systems and the values in the CLNP Security Option. [The Blacker Front End (BFE) is one example of such a trusted device.] These devices may receive CLNP PDUs which are in range for the intermediate device, but are either not within the accredited range for the source or the destination. In the former case, the PDU should be treated as described in Paragraph 6.6. In the latter case, a CLNP Error Report PDU should be sent to the originating CLNP entity. The first octet of the Reason for Discard parameter should be set to 1101 0010. This code indicates to the originating CLNP entity that communication with the end system is administratively prohibited (refer to Table 6.1). The security range of the interface on which the reply will be sent determines whether a reply is allowed and at what security level it should be sent.
contents.html_ja: インターネットワーク内の特定の装置は、2 つのエンドシステム間の通信が許可されていることを検証する仲介者として機能する場合があります。この判断は、エンドシステムについての知識と、CLNP セキュリティオプションの値の組み合わせに基づきます。［Blacker Front End（BFE）は、そのような信頼できる装置の一例です。］これらの装置は、仲介装置にとっては範囲内ですが、送信元または宛先の認定範囲内にはない CLNP PDU を受信する場合があります。前者の場合、PDU は第 6.6 項に記述されたとおりに扱うべきです。後者の場合は、元の CLNP エンティティに CLNP エラーレポート PDU を送信すべきです。破棄理由パラメータの最初のオクテットは 1101 0010 に設定すべきです。このコードは、元の CLNP エンティティに、エンドシステムとの通信が管理上禁止されていることを示します（表 6.1 を参照）。応答の送信が許可されるかどうか、および応答をどのセキュリティレベルで送信すべきかは、応答が送信されるインタフェースのセキュリティ範囲によって決まります。

contents.html: "The Need for Release Markings in the GOSIP Standard Security Label" (Position Paper), Tom Bartee (IC Staff)
contents.html_ja: "The Need for Release Markings in the GOSIP Standard Security Label"（意見書）、Tom Bartee（IC Staff）
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。寄稿の区切りページの題名

contents.html: POSITION PAPER ON THE NEED FOR RELEASE MARKINGS IN THE GOSIP STANDARD SECURITY LABEL
contents.html_ja: GOSIP 標準セキュリティラベルにおける公開許可マーキングの必要性に関する意見書
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

contents.html: This is a position paper concerning the use of inverted bit-map release markings as a mechanism for labeling classified data in the Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. The position taken is that because of the widespread usage of release attributes in Government systems inclusion of this labeling technique would be desirable.
contents.html_ja: これは、政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル向けの標準セキュリティラベルにおいて、機密データにラベルを付ける仕組みとして、反転ビットマップによる公開許可マーキングを使用することに関する意見書です。示される立場は、政府のシステムでは公開許可属性が広く使われていることから、このラベル付けの手法を含めることが望ましいというものです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

contents.html: Examples of release attributes include country and NATO release markings, markings for release to selected contractors (corporations) in certain programs, releases to LEAs and DEA in DOD and Intelligence counter-narcotics programs, etc.
contents.html_ja: 公開許可属性の例には、国および NATO の公開許可マーキング、特定のプログラムにおける選定された請負業者（企業）への公開許可マーキング、国防総省および情報機関の麻薬対策プログラムにおける LEA と DEA への公開許可などがあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

contents.html: When two bit-map markings for (normal) restrictive attributes are combined, the two bit-maps are ORed bit-by-bit as follows.
contents.html_ja: （通常の）制限的属性のための 2 つのビットマップマーキングを組み合わせる場合、2 つのビットマップは、次のようにビットごとに OR されます。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す
原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ビット列の図を原本画像から等幅で起こす（矢印は → で表す）

contents.html: this gives a lattice least-upper-bound. For the above the leftmost label shows B and C attributes and the rightmost A and C attributes so the resulting label should indicate the combined attributes A and B and C.
contents.html_ja: これは、束（lattice）の最小上界を与えます。上の例では、左端のラベルは B と C の属性を示し、右端のラベルは A と C の属性を示すため、結果のラベルは A と B と C を合わせた属性を示すべきです。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す（文頭の小文字は原本どおり）

contents.html: When ORing is tried for release attribute markings it does not give the desired result.
contents.html_ja: 公開属性のマーキングに OR を試みると、望ましい結果になりません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

||||
ABCD   ABCD   ABCD

contents.html: The above indicates that a label indicating a release to B and C when combined with a label indicating a release to A and C provides for release to A and B and C while, in fact, the release should be to C only.
contents.html_ja: 上の例は、B と C への公開許可を示すラベルを、A と C への公開許可を示すラベルと組み合わせると、A と B と C への公開許可になることを示しますが、実際には、C のみに公開許可すべきです。

contents.html_ja: 0 が公開許可を、1 が公開許可がないことを示す反転ビットを使用すると、結果は次のようになります

contents.html:
1001   0101 → 1101
||||
ABCD   ABCD   ABCD
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ビット列の図を原本画像（scale 4）から起こす

contents.html: The leftmost label is for release to B and C and the middle label indicates a release to A and C, the result is that the object is releasable only to C which is what is desired.
contents.html_ja: 左端のラベルは B と C への公開許可を、中央のラベルは A と C への公開許可を示しており、その結果、オブジェクトは C にのみ公開許可可能となり、これが望ましい結果です。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す（p.150 冒頭の続きを含む）

contents.html: The inverted bit-map markings can also be used in implementing Mandatory Access Control. The user is given a label with 0s in the positions where the release attribute markings indicating his affiliations occur (if the user is British a 0 is in the British position, if employed by Boeing a 0 is in the Boeing position, etc.) and 1s are placed in the other positions. When the label associated with a user is ORed with a label on a data item, the presence of a 0 in the result indicates the data has been released to the user.
contents.html_ja: 反転ビットマップのマーキングは、強制アクセス制御の実装にも使用できます。利用者には、その所属を示す公開許可属性マーキングが現れる位置に 0 を、その他の位置に 1 を置いたラベルが与えられます（利用者が英国人であれば英国の位置に 0 を、Boeing に勤務していれば Boeing の位置に 0 を置く、など）。利用者に関連付けられたラベルをデータ項目のラベルと OR したとき、結果に 0 があれば、そのデータが利用者に公開許可されていることを示します。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

contents.html: The inverted bit-map technique has been used in several operational systems and is included in the DCI Extended Security Option for the IP header. It is also used in the CMW program. Its virtue is its simple operation and conceptual neatness. While labels can be used with non-inverted release markings, programs must "know" which bits are the release bits and process them differently.
contents.html_ja: 反転ビットマップの手法は、複数の運用システムで使われており、IP ヘッダ向けの DCI 拡張セキュリティオプションにも含まれています。また、CMW プログラムでも使われています。その長所は、動作が単純で、概念が整然としていることです。ラベルは反転していない公開許可マーキングでも使えますが、その場合、プログラムはどのビットが公開許可ビットであるかを「知って」おり、それらを別に処理しなければなりません。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。ドットプリンタ印字の OCR 誤りを原本画像（scale 2・4）と語ごとに照合して直す

contents.html: The inclusion of an inverted bit map marking scheme for release attributes as one of the Security Tag Types in the standard would be useful to a large body of Government (and Commercial) users.
contents.html_ja: 公開許可属性のための反転ビットマップマーキング方式を、標準のセキュリティタグ型の 1 つとして含めることは、多数の政府（および民間）の利用者にとって有用です。

On April 9 and 10, 1991 the Protocol Security Group at NIST held its Second Workshop on Security Labels. Forty representatives from the U.S. Government, Industry, and the Canadian Government gathered for two days to discuss a NIST proposed Standard Security Label for the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. Issues on security policy and security object registration were also discussed in reference to the proposed label. The information shared during the two days of discussion and the recommendations of the group are documented in these proceedings.
Papers are contributions of the authors and do not necessarily represent NIST views.

Robert Rosenthal, Manager of the Protocol Security Group at NIST, welcomed the attendees. He described the role of this workshop in NIST's effort to incorporate security mechanisms into the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. Mr. Rosenthal envisions a set of Government OSI Security Profiles that will be pointed to by the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 146, GOSIP. The first set of profiles would include the following topics:
Key Management for Public Key Cryptography . Security Protocol for Layer 4 (SP4) . Security Labels . Cryptographic Modules . Register for Uniquely Named Managed Security Objects .
Mr. Rosenthal introduced Noel Nazario (NIST) Workshop Chair. Mr.
Nazario reviewed the agenda and asked the attendees to introduce themselves. Appendix A contains a list of attendees.

Larry Keys (NIST), will be the Registrar for NIST's Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR) The CSOR is being organized . using ANSI/ISO guidelines for object registration. Mr. Keys gave a status report on the work done so far in setting up this service and outlined the basics of the registration procedure.

George Rogers (IC Staff) asked whether this register could or would register classified objects. Dr. Dennis Branstad (NIST) answered that NIST has no authority over classified information. Branstad added that since the register deals with a hierarchical structure the "classified side" could be treated as a branch of the same tree structure. Mr. Rogers expressed concern with having more than one register and recommended avoiding this situation if possible.

Dr. Stuart Katzke (NIST) spoke about the relationship between security labels and data categorization. Data is categorized according to the protection required thus reflecting the risks involved in their loss and misuse. Some issues in this area are:
Types of categories: Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
Structural relationship between categories: Hierarchical (e.g., DoD Model for Confidentiality), Lattice, Independent.

Independence between data categorization structure and access control models such as Access Control Lists, Bell and LaPadula/Clearances, Capabilities, Chinese Wall, and Biba. Interpretation of categories as they relate to protection objectives, (e.g.. No consensus on an interpretation of hierarchical integrity categories.)
Implementation and enforcement of data categorization policy.
Consistent interpretation of protection objectives by the
organization receiving the data. Variation of protection objectives based upon
organization receiving the data, (e.g.. Modification may be done by agency X while only read access is permitted to agency Y)
Ancestry How much needs to known about the data
generation, change, and disposition ancestry to protect them properly. What are the protection requirements on this ancestry information.
Dr. Katzke gave a historical perspective of efforts made in addressing the data categorization problem. Some important events weres
Work was initiated at NIST in the early 70s by Branstad and Katzke

Subcommittee on Automated Information Systems Security/National Telecommunications and Information System Security Committee (SAISS/NTISSC Their work resulted in ) coining the term "Sensitive Unclassified”.
Computer Security Act: Adopted the term "Sensitive Unclassified”. The act gave no guidance for determining the degree of sensitivity.

Computer and Telecommunications Security Council (CTSC) Warren Schmitt presented to the CTSC his categorization model. This model consists of three levels (Low, Medium, High) along three axes (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) The
resulting matrix is then mapped to the appropriate mechanisms.
NIST*s First Invitational Workshop on Security Labels for Open Systems was held on May 30 and 31, 1990. The proceedings were published as NISTIR 4362.
Computer Systems Security and Privacy Advisory Board: Presentations on Data Categorization Requirements and Approach based on initiatives by:
. . Specific Federal Agencies (e.g. Census Bureau, IRS,
Matching Programs) Federal Agencies under Bilateral Agreements
So far all discussions on the subject have lead to "black holes" (i.e.. No general agreement has been achieved). Potential actions
that could result in uniform data categories for the federal government include:
Office of Management and Budget (0MB) policy decisions
Selection of categories within major Department of
Defense efforts such as the Corporate Information Management (CIM) and/or Computer-aided Acquisition and Logistics Support (CALS)
Dr. Katzke concluded his presentation by recommending that this workshop focus on the less controversial part of the problem (i.e., Agreeing on a label format)
Noel Nazario (NIST) summarized the developments in the labeling effort since the previous workshop. These include:
The publication of the proceedings of the May 1990 labeling workshop as NISTIR 4362, "Security Labels for Open Systems an Invitational Workshop .
A panel session at the 13th National Computer Security Conference chaired by Dr. Dennis Branstad (NIST) This
session included the participation of Russ Housley (Xerox) Warren Schmitt (Sears Technology Services) and Noel Nazario
The release for comment of an initial proposal for a security label based on the output of the first labeling workshop.
Interaction with the Trusted Systems Interoperability Group (TSIG) developers of the Commercial Internet Protocol
Presentation on NIST's GOSIP labeling effort at the Workshop on Database Security Labeling for Civilian Agencies in Tucson, Arizona.
The decision by NIST to establish and maintain a Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR)
The release for comment of the initial draft of a Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) specifying a Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile.
Ron Sharp (AT&T) represented the Trusted Systems Interoperability Group (TSIG) Mr. Sharp described the TSIG as a very informal

group of implementors interested in developing interoperable trusted distributed systems. The TSIG is engaged in projects such as CIPSO, Trusted X-Windows, Trusted Network File Systems (NFS), Trusted Session Management, and Trusted Sockets. The current focus for TSIG members is the TCP/IP communications protocol but the door remains open for a transition to OSI as markets emerge. In developing CIPSO the TSIG adopted and modified original work done by Sun Microsystems and Hewlett-Packard. The group has spawned an Internet Working Group whose purpose is to present CIPSO as an Internet Request for Comment (RFC) Mr. Sharp enumerated reasons . for the development of CIPSO, its main features, and presented the label format. His presentation slides and the current version of the CIPSO specification appears on page 55 of this document.
Noel Nazario presented the Standard Security Label (SSL) The

specification for this label is given by the initial draft of a FIPS, called Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. This document provides the format of a security label that may be used at different layers of the OSI architecture. The semantics of the label will be given by a Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR) This future FIPS will
be referenced by the U. S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP) when describing labeling options for various protocols.

The SSL begins with a Security Label Indicator and a length field indicating the length of the Security Information that follows. The Security Information field includes a Register Index Code (RIC) a Security Level field, and Security Tags. The RIC

identifies the semantic rules for the label as registered in the CSOR. There are four tag types, one of which indicates the end of the label. The other three tag types may be used to carry additional security information. The presentation slides on page 21 of this report illustrate the general format of the label and the four tag types. A full description appears in the draft FIPS text also included.

Mr. Nazario compared the label option currently specified by GOSIP for the Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) to the SSL. The GOSIP CLNP security option is actually two separate options defined by two different authorities or activities while the SSL can provide the same information in a label defined by a single authority. The Classification Protection Level in the Basic Security Option (BSO) is analogous to the Security Level field in the SSL. The equivalent of the Additional Security Information in the Extended Security Option (ESO) can be provided by the three information-carrying tag types in the SSL.

Mr. Nazario also compared the SSL to the Commercial CIPSO. There are two main distinctions between the CIPSO label and the SSL. The Domain of Interpretation field that identifies the defining authority for the CIPSO label is a four octet fixed length field while the RIC, which points to the semantics of the label as registered in the CSOR for the SSL, is a variable length field. The second difference is that every CIPSO tag has a security level field while there is only one security level field in the SSL.
Noel Nazario also presented proposed modifications to the text in
of the U.S. Government Open Systems
Interconnection Profile (GOSIP) Chapter 6 of GOSIP currently . contains the specification for a security option for the Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) This chapter is also a

placeholder for future specifications. Changes include a new paragraph structure to accommodate a NIST Security Information option for CLNP and placeholders for security parameters at other layers. Only a label parameter is currently defined within the NIST Security Information option. A pointer to the SSL document provides the format specification for this label parameter. The new text also points to the Computer Security Objects Register (CSOR) to provide the semantics for the label. The new CLNP Security Parameter allows the use of either the existent BSO/ESO label or the NIST Security Information. The BSO/ESO was kept for backwards compatibility.
Wayne Jansen (NIST) presented an overview of Security Labels at the Transport Layer. His discussion dealt with the Transport Layer Security Protocol (TLSP) The TLSP, currently under development

within ISO, is being balloted for CD (Committee Draft) status. Mr. Jansen compared the SSL and the TLSP label formats and their respective views on label registration. The presentation suggested a compromise format for the alignment of both labels and a methodology for creating label definitions independent of encoding concerns using ASN.l.

Russ Housley (Xerox) presented comments on the draft Standard Security Label document. The proposed label may be applicable to several protocols within the OSI architecture. However, an ASN.l definition would be necessary for use at layer 7. The IEEE 802.2 working group is currently working on a layer 2 label, it would be appropriate to present the SSL to that group. Mr. Housley added that there should be a reference in the SSL text that indicates what document provides usage rules for this label. The full text of the Xerox comments appear later in this document.

Hilary Hosmer (Data Security) presented the concept of multipolicy. She pointed out that OSI security labels should be able to support co-existing security policies Ms. Hosmer stated that allowing . only one Security Level field in the SSL is a serious limitation because it makes it difficult to support multiple security policies.

David Crawford (Canadian Defense) discussed Canada *s coexisting security policies. He explained the relationship between security levels that cover the equivalents to U.S. Classified and Unclassified but Sensitive.
Thomas Bartee (IC Staff) presented a position paper justifying a request for an additional tag type for the Standard Security Label (SSL) Mr. Bartee *s argument was that the tags currently specified

in the SSL are geared towards indicating restriction markings. The addition of a "reversed” bit map type would make it easier to specify permissive markings such as release indicators. He mentioned that such an approach is currently used in the Director of Central Intelligence Office (DCI) Extended IP Security Option and by the Compartmented Workstation program.

Most of the second day of the workshop was devoted to discussion of issues raised in the presentations of the first day. The group listed and prioritized the different issues. This ordered list guided the discussion of the relevant topics. After discussing each issue an informal vote was taken. The position taken by the group was recorded as the workshop's output. That output is presented in the following section.

The following list of issues were identified and discussed by the workshop attendees. The statements listed under each issue were subject to an informal vote and represent the group's position. This list constitutes the workshop's output.
The option to expand sizes and add tag types should be left open
Focus the use of labels at layers 3, 4, 2 and 7.
It should be specified that the ASN.l definition provided applies to layer 7 while the format given in the SSL document applies to layers 3, 4, and 2,
The Usage section in the SSL document should specify that the label applies to the data unit.
The Usage section should include a pointer to the source for exception processing rules.
Given that the length of the Index will always appear after the label Indicator the RIC Indicator should be eliminated.
Length value 255 should be reserved for future use.
The Security Level field should be eliminated in favor of a Security Level Tag Type.
A single label with multiple RIC-tag sets should be allowed as opposed to multiple labels.
No multi-octet length fields should be allowed for layers 2, 3f and 4.
All [tag] lengths should be allowed to go up to 255.
Placing of the SSL within GOSIP
The use of BSO/ESO should be mutually exclusive with the NIST Security Information [in CLNP]
BSO/ESO should only be supported by CLNP [for backwards compatibility]
The Null Tag Type should be eliminated.
An additional length field should be used to support multiple RIC-tag sets.
Usage of terms should be revised for consistency and all definitions should be included in the document.
A tag type for permisive functionality should be added.
The Standard Security Label should provide for multiple instantiations of RICs followed by their respective tags.

This Standard specifies the format for a security label for the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). This network security label tells protocol processing entities how to handle unclassified but sensitive data communicated between open systems. Information carried by this label can be used to control access, specify protective measures, and indicate additional handling restrictions required by a network security policy.
Key words: ADP security, GOSIP security, network security labels, secure Open Systems
Federal Information Processing Standard Publication xxx
Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile

Federal Information Processing Standards are issued by the National Institute of Standards and Technology pursuant of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949, as amended. Public Law 89-306 (79 Stat 1127), Executive Order 11717 (38 FR 12315, dated May 11, 1973), and Part 6 of Title 15 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR).
Name of Standard: Standard Security Label for Government Open Systems Interconnection Profiles.
Category of Standard: ADP Operations, Computer Security.

Explanation: This Standard specifies the format for a security Label within the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP). Security labels indicate data sensitivity to accidental, unauthorized, intentional, or malicious disclosure, modification and destruction. Labels are used to control access, specify protective measures, and indicate handling restrictions requked by a network security policy.

The label presented here contains a security level indicator and security tags that may carry compartments, caveats, and handling restrictions. Four security tag types provide for a bit map, two enumerated set representations (set inclusion and set exclusion), and a free form field.
Maintenance Agency: Computer Systems Laboratory, National Institute of Stanctods and Technology.

Scope: This standard specifies a security label for GOSIP compliant implementations. The specified label may be used as a security feature at different layers of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The specification given here is limited to the syntactic aspect of the label. The semantics of security labels, as defined for different security domains. are given by a Security Objects Register. Appendix B contains an example semantic definition for a label.

Applicability: The specified label applies to OSI network systems handling U.S. Government unclassified but sensitive data. This includes use by government agencies and commercial organizations conducting business with the Federal government.

Applications: The specified security label shall be used by OSI protocol processing entities to control access, specify protective measures and indicate handling restrictions required by a network security policy.
Implementations: Complying implementations shall be capable of transmitting, receiving, and handling the label format specified in this document
Implementation Schedule: This standard becomes effective ...
Specifications: Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS xxx) Standard for Information Security Labels (affixed).
Comments: Comments and questions may be addressed to:

U.S. Government agencies are required to protect information assets essential to their operations. This includes both the protection of information within computer systems and while in transit over communications networks. This standard defines a network security label for use with the U.S. Government Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Profile (GOSIP; FIPS PUB XXX).

The security label specified here can indicate data sensitivity to accidental, unauthorized, intentional, or malicious disclosure, modification and destruction. This label format shall be used by Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile (GOSIP) implementations to provide security information to protocol processing entities. The format for the GOSIP security label is shown in figure 4.1.
This figure identifies three fields, Security Label Indicator, Length Indicator, and Security Information.
Format Network Information Security Label Fig. 4.1
The size of the Security Label Indicator (SLI) field is 1 octet. The value of the SLI is 1100 4.4 0000 (CO hex).
The size of the Length Indicator (LI) field is 1 octet. This is the length of the Security Information Field. The value of the LI ranges between 8 and 128 octets.

The variable length Security Information (SI) field contains the security label. This field is shown in Figure 4.2. The SI field contains the Register Index Code, a Security Level, and one or more Security Tags.

A Register Index Code (RIC) field points to the semantic definition of the label as registered in a Security Objects Register. The RIC is a variable size field. This field includes the RIC Indicator, RIC Length, and the Index field. 1.1
4.4.1.2 The size of the RIC Indicator (RIC-Ind) field is 1 octet. The binary value of this field is 1100 1010 (CA hex).
The size of the RIC Length Indicator (RIC-LI) field is 1 octet. Its value is the length of the Index (I) field in octets.

The encoding of the index is given by the Security Objects Register. In the case when only part of an octet is required for encoding the index the significant bits will be left-justified and padded with 0.
The size of the Security Level (SL) field is 1 octet, values range from 0 to 255. There is only one SL per label.

Additional security information is conveyed using Security Tags. A single label may have multiple variable size tags. Each Security Tag has fixed size type and length fields plus a variable size information field. The value of the length field in Tag Type 0 is zero; it contains no information.

The size of the Additional Security Tag Type (TT) field is 1 octet. Its value indicates the tag type. Values range between 0 and 255. This standard defines tag types 0 through 4, all other tag types are reserved for definition by NIST’s Security Objects Register. At least one tag must be present in every label.

The size of the Additional Security Tag Length (TL) is 1 octet. The TL indicates the length of the information in the tag. Its value ranges between 0 and 30 octets. Note: This field is always zero for Tag Type 0.

This variable length field contains the value of the Security Tag. This document describes this field for Tag Types 1-4. Note: This field is not defined for Tag Type 0. All other tag types are reserved for definition by NIST’s Security Objects Register.
Null tag, indicates end of the label. One (1) and only one (1) Tag Type 0 shall be present in any security label.
The format of tag 0 is as follows:

The information carried by this tag is interpreted as a bit map of security attributes. The complete set of possible attributes is represented and those that apply are explicidy indicated. Length field values range between 1 and 30 octets.
In the bit map a bit N is set to 1 if attribute N (as defined in the register), is part of the label
it is 0 if attribute is not part of the label. Bits shall be numbered starting with the most significant bit of the first transmitted octet. Unused bits at the end the last octet are set to 0 .
The format of this tag type is as follows:
Tag Type Tag Length Bit Map

Tag type 2 is used when only a few security attributes out of a large set apply to a protocol data unit (PDU). This is done by enumerating the attributes that apply (set inclusion). This enumeration shall start with the lowest numbered attribute following an ascending order. TL field values range between 2 and 30 octets.
A single tag may enumerate up to 15 security attributes, assigning 2 octets per attribute. The value for a security attribute may be between 0 and 65535.
The format of this tag type is as follows:
Tag type 3 is used when only a few security attributes out of a large set do not apply to a
message. This is done by enumerating the attributes that do not apply to the
exclusion). Length field values range between 2 and 30 octets.
A single tag may enumerate up to 15 security attributes, assigning 2 octets per category. The value of each category can be from 0-65535.
The format of this tag type is as follows:
Tag type 4 carries a free format field of up to 30 octets. The information field of this tag may hold character strings, or any user-defined data. Length field values range between 1 and 30 octets.
The format of this tag type is as follows:
At most 1 security label may be used per layer PDU. The label described here shall be copied upon fragmentation. All multi-octet fields are defined to be transmitted in network byte order.

At least one tag must be present in every label. If no additional security information is required a NULL tag (Type 0) will be used. Only 1 NULL tag may appear in any label, it indicates the end of the label. The failure to find a NULL tag when expected and/or the finding of such tag when not expected are security relevant events that must be reported.

Multiple tags of types other than 0 may be present in a label. The detection of a label with information outside of the range permitted by the communicating parties must be reported as a security relevant event.

Security is of fundamental importance to the acceptance and use of open systems in the U.S. Government. Part 2 of the Open Systems Interconnection reference model (Security Architecture) is now an International Standard (IS 7498/2) The standard describes a . general architecture for security in OSI, defines a set of security services that may be supported within the OSI model, and outlines a number of mechanisms than can be used in providing the services. However, no protocols, formats or minimum requirements are contained in the standard.
The text below describes security options that may be specified when incorporating security services to OSI Network and Transport Layers This chapter does not describe at this time a complete set

of security options that a user might desire nor a description of the security services and protocols that are associated with the specified parameters. Security labels are parameters that have been identified as needed if certain security services (e.g., confidentiality, access control) are incorporated to the OSI Layers. This chapter should be considered as a placeholder for future security specifications. Appendix provides further
information on what specifications are considered needed for OSI security

As defined by ISO, security features are considered both implementation and usage options. An organization desiring security in a product that is being purchased in accordance with this profile must specify the security services required, the placement of the services within the OSI architecture, the mechanisms to provide the services and the management features required.

The implementation of the security option requires assigning new parameter values to the Reason for Discard parameter in the CLNP Error Report PDU. The first octet of the parameter value contains an error type code as described in IS 8473. Values beyond those assigned in the standard are shown in Table 6.1. The second octet of the Reason for Discard parameter value either locates the error in the discarded PDU or contains the value zero as described in the standard
Table 6.1 Extended Values in the Reason For Discard Parameter
6.2.1 OSI Application and Presentation Layer Security Parameter
6.2.2 OSI Transport and Network Layer Security Parameter

IS 8473 defines the format of the Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) security parameter. This parameter consists of the three fields shown in Table 6.2. IS 8073, the Connection Oriented Transport Protocol Specification, leaves the definition of the security parameter to the user. The following specification shall be used by both protocols.
IS 8473 assigns the value ”1100 0101” to the Parameter Code field to identify the parameter as the Security Option.
This octet indicates the length, in octets, of the Parameter Value field

The Parameter Value field contains the security information. IS 8473 defines only the first octet of the Parameter Value field. This section completes the definition of this field. Table 6.3 illustrates the format of the Parameter Value field within the Security Parameter.

As described in IS 8473, the high order two bits of the first octet of the Parameter Value field specify the Security Format Code. The standard reserves the remaining six bits and specifies that they must be zero.
The values of the Security Format Code are:
01 Source Address Specific 10 Destination Address Specific 11 Globally Unique

The Basic Security Option of the Security Parameter identifies the U.S. Department of Defense classification level to which a PDU is to be protected and the authorities whose protection rules apply to that PDU. This option may appear at most once in a PDU. When the Basic Security Option appears in the Security Parameter of a PDU, it must be the first option in the Parameter Value field. This parameter may not be used together with the NIST Security Option. Section 6.2.3 defines the format of the Basic Security Option.

The Extended Security Option permits additional security labelling information beyond that present in the Basic Security Option. This extended information is supplied in a CLNP or Connection Oriented Transport PDU to meet the needs of registered authorities. This option may appear at most once in a PDU. The Extended Security Option must follow the Basic Option if it is present in the Security Parameter Value field. If an authority requires this option for a specific system, it must be specified explicitly in any Request for Proposal for that system. This parameter may not be used together with the NIST Security Option. Paragraph 6.2.4 defines the format of the Extended Option.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Security Option provides for a number of network security related parameters. The NIST Security Label is the only parameter type currently defined under this option. This parameter is specified in FIPS PUB XXX, Standard Security Label for the Government Open Systems Interconnection Profile. The NIST Security Label parameter provides a security level indicator and security information tags to convey security information on CLNP or Connection Oriented Transport PDUs NIST reserves all other NIST Security Option

parameter types. The security label parameter option may appear at most once in a PDU. This parameter may not be used together with the Basic and/or Extended Security Options. If this option is required by an authority for a specific system, it must be specified explicitly in any Request for Proposal for that system. Paragraph 6.2.5 defines the format of the NIST Security Option.
The Basic Security Option is used by the components of an internetwork to:
A. Transmit from source to destination, in a network standard representation, the common DoD security labels.
B. Validate the PDU as appropriate for transmission from the source and delivery to the destination.
C. Ensure that the route taken by the PDU is protected to the level required by all protection authorities indicated on the PDU.
Table 6.4 shows the format of the Basic Security Option.
The value of this field identifies this as the Basic Security Option
This length field, when present, indicates the length, in octets, of the Basic Information field. The Basic Information field is variable in length and has a minimum length of two octets.
The Basic Information field consists of two subfields as Table 6.5 illustrates

The Classification Level field specifies the U.S. DoD classification level to which the PDU must be protected. The information in the PDU must be treated at this level unless it is regraded in accordance under the procedures of all the authorities identified by the Protection Authority Flags. The field is one octet in length. Table 6.6 provides the encodings for this field.

The Protection Authority Flags field indicates the National Access Program (s) or Special Access Program (s) whose rules apply to the protection of the PDU. Its field length and source flags are described below. Each format code is assigned to a specific controlling activity. A single controlling activity may be responsible for multiple format codes. However, a particular format code may appear at most once in a PDU. Certain devices in an internetwork may act as intermediaries to validate that communications between two end systems is authorized. [The Blacker Front End (BFE) is one example of such a trusted device.] These devices may receive CLNP PDUs which are in range for the intermediate device^ but are either not within the accredited range for the source or the destination.
